title: The Four's Ordinance
tagline: Oaths spoken, offices kept, ledgers checked, and the letter that claims to be law
description: Paris in the year of the diamond studs. A civics-and-rhetoric adventure through Dumas's France where power moves by oath, office, and purse, rhetoric wins scenes, and the sealed lettre tests whether law or favour shall have the last word.
worldPrompt: An original civics adventure after Alexandre Dumas's The Three Musketeers (1844, public domain). The learner is the honest clerk of the four: d'Artagnan, Athos, Porthos, Aramis, with Treville, Richelieu, and Milady testing their tests. Each chapter gates the history and civics unit: personal versus institutional power, oaths as constitutions, rhetoric devices, fiscal centralisation and ledgers, blank lettres versus rule of law and separation of powers, and a written ordinance with a test lettre case. Tone is grave about law and lively about Dumas. Loot is 17th century French life: rapier hilt, sealed lettre, treasury ledger, innkeeper's bill.

characters.name: d'Artagnan
characters.bio: Young, fast, learning to choose when honour and interest pull apart. You counsel him before he draws.

characters.name: Athos
characters.bio: Nobly born, grieved, exacting about oaths. He asks what must costs and who pays it.

characters.name: Porthos
characters.bio: Big heart and big appetite for pay and praise. He checks whether courage has a budget.

characters.name: Aramis
characters.bio: Pious and plotting. In late Dumas he is the reminder that a sacred vow claimed for a scheme is still a scheme.

characters.name: Cardinal Richelieu
characters.bio: Brilliant centraliser. His sealed lettre is the test: necessity asked as favour versus law's answer.

chapters.title: Whose France Is It?
chapters.hook: King, cardinal, captains. Ask who pays and who writes the record.

chapters.title: The Words You Swear
chapters.hook: All for one. Say who is bound, to what, at what price must means.

chapters.title: How Speeches Move Us
chapters.hook: Ethos, pathos, logos. Deliberative or forensic. Anaphora, antithesis, and what is missing.

chapters.title: Who Can Pay the March?
chapters.hook: The innkeeper waits. A lord's purse runs out. A ministry's ledger does not, until it fails its audit.

chapters.title: The Lettre That Says It Is Law
chapters.hook: A seal that pre-excuses. Law that must bind even the hand that holds the seal.

chapters.title: Write the Ordinance
chapters.hook: Name your oath, set your offices, keep your ledger, and test the lettre before you obey it.

loot.name: Oath Ribbon
loot.description: The ribbon four men touched when they said all for one. Who, what, at what cost. Chapter 2, the oath.

loot.name: Rapier Hilt
loot.description: Cross and guard, honour where it costs. Chapter 2, the quarrel of motives.

loot.name: Sealed Lettre
loot.description: A folded sheet with a great seal that says all is for the state. The claim to test against law and process. Chapter 5, the cardinal's test.

loot.name: Treasury Ledger
loot.description: Where taxes to one account and pay by office can be counted and audited. Chapter 4, fiscal France.

loot.name: Innkeeper's Bill
loot.description: Supper, horse, and march charged and receipted. The small record that proves whether favour or institution fed the company. Chapter 4, the march.

loot.name: Ordinance Seal
loot.description: The Four's seal when oath, offices, ledger, dispute steps, and lettre judgement are written and hold. Legendary ordinance clear.
